note: Spoken intros of the trajectory-trace videos (tools/render_attractor_trace.py --intro), rewritten 19 Oct 2026 (human: 'review the script it's out of date and really could use some love'). Facts: f64-strong and takens-strong are the cell alpha 0.07248, log10 T -0.148 (chaotic); the Takens observable is log p_max with three delays; p8-approach-f32 is alpha 0.0734, log10 T -0.148, where trajectories fall onto an attracting period-8 cycle writing 'This is there is a is a.'
chaotic: This is a strange attractor of a language model talking to itself. At every step the model, Qwen two point five with half a billion parameters, reads back its own expected next word, a blend of word embeddings weighted by how likely each word is, and produces the next one. Each speck of light is a state of this loop, colored by the word it is about to write. The bright dot follows a single trajectory. Watch it jump from state to state, and listen to the words it writes. Two trajectories that begin almost together soon write different texts: nearby states separate exponentially. That is what chaos means.
takens: Here is the same chaotic loop, rebuilt from the outside. We keep only one number per step: how confident the model is in its top word, the logarithm of its largest probability. Plotting each value against the next two, a method due to Floris Takens, brings back the shape of the attractor without looking inside the model. The dot follows one trajectory through this reconstruction, and you hear each word as it is written.
p8: Not every setting of the loop is chaotic. A small step away, with slightly stronger steering, the same picture holds a cycle of eight states that pulls trajectories in. The dot starts among the scattered states of the approach, wanders, and is captured. From then on it visits the same eight points in turn, and the words repeat: This is there is a is a. Order, from the same model, a small step away from chaos.
